h1: Web development for San Francisco companies that have outgrown their site
intro: We design and build websites for San Francisco companies: marketing sites your team can update without an engineer, redesigns and migrations that keep your search rankings, client portals with documents and payments, and ongoing care and security. Every build is accessible, fast, and set up so consent and tracking follow California privacy law.

sections.h: The site was built for the company you were two years ago
p: Most Bay Area companies we meet have a site that made sense at the seed stage: a homepage, a pricing page and a blog that nobody updates because every change needs a developer. Since then the product has new features, the buyer is now a VP rather than a founder, and the sales team keeps sending prospects a PDF because the site does not say what they need.

The web development San Francisco companies need at this stage fixes that without throwing away what works. The pages that rank keep their addresses or get proper redirects. Marketing gets a CMS it can use. Engineering gets its time back.

sections.h: California rules every Bay Area site should meet
p: Three legal risks shape how we build sites for California companies. First, the California Consumer Privacy Act: your site needs a working "Do Not Sell or Share" option where it applies, a privacy policy that matches what the site actually collects, and support for the Global Privacy Control signal that browsers send. Second, accessibility: website accessibility claims are common in California, often brought under the ADA together with the state's Unruh Civil Rights Act. Third, tracking: chat widgets, session recording and ad pixels have drawn lawsuits under the California Invasion of Privacy Act.
We are not lawyers, but we build to WCAG accessibility standards, load trackers only after consent where your counsel says so, and keep a list of every script on the site.

sections.h: How a build runs: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we review your current site, analytics and search data, and interview sales to learn what prospects ask. Plan: sitemap, page briefs, redirect map and a written launch date. Build: design, content and development in parallel, with your team reviewing on a staging site. Grow: after launch we watch rankings, fix anything that dropped, and keep improving the pages that bring in leads.

faqs.q: Which CMS suits a San Francisco SaaS company?
faqs.a: It depends on who edits the site and what it needs to connect to. WordPress suits content-heavy sites and teams that need many plugins. A headless CMS with Next.js suits companies with engineers who want the site in their own stack. We recommend one after seeing your team and your content plan.

faqs.q: Will a redesign hurt our Google rankings?
faqs.a: It should not, if it is planned properly. Before launch we map every ranking URL to its new address, carry over titles and metadata, and set redirects. After launch we monitor rankings and crawl errors and fix any drops quickly. Most ranking losses after redesigns come from skipped redirect work, and we do not skip it.

Yes. We build to WCAG standards: keyboard navigation, color contrast, labeled forms, alt text and screen reader testing. Accessibility claims are common in California, so it matters for risk as well as for your users. We can also audit your current site and fix the issues we find before or instead of a redesign.

faqs.q: How do you handle cookie consent and CCPA on the site?
faqs.a: We set up a consent tool that respects the Global Privacy Control signal, add the opt-out links that apply to your business, and load ad and analytics scripts according to the rules your counsel sets. We document every tracking script and what it collects, which makes your privacy policy easier to keep accurate.

faqs.q: Do you meet San Francisco clients in person during a website project?
faqs.a: Most website projects run well remotely. We work from London with teams across four regions, and review calls happen in the Pacific morning. If a kickoff workshop or a content day with your team needs us in the room, we plan a visit when the project needs it.

faqs.q: How long does a website project take?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of templates, who writes the copy and how much content moves across. A focused marketing site is quicker than a redesign with hundreds of blog posts and a portal. We set a written launch date in the plan, and the Signal Lead tells you early if anything on either side puts it at risk.

faqs.q: Can you look after the site after launch?
faqs.a: Yes. Our website care plans cover updates, backups, uptime and security monitoring, small changes and monthly checks on speed and search. You keep full ownership of the site, the hosting account and the domain. If you would rather run it in house, we hand over with documentation and training.
